title: New Nintendo 3DS XL 2015 Circle Pad Replacement
author: Tori Anderson

lines: Fully power off the console and flip it upside down.
Remove the game card, headphones, charging cable, stylus, and anything else connected.

steps.title: Remove the back cover
lines: Use a JIS 00 screwdriver to loosen the two black captive screws on the back cover.
Gently pry the tabs on the side of the device with a spudger or your thumbnail to release the clips securing the back cover.

steps.title: Remove the microSD card
lines: Push the microSD card in to eject it, then remove it.

steps.title: Remove the battery
lines: Hold the console securely in one hand, with the battery facing up.
Flip the console over so the battery falls out into your other hand.

steps.title: Lift the bottom cover
lines: Use the point of a spudger or thumb tack to pry out the two rubber bumpers on the back of the device.
Use a JIS 00 screwdriver to remove all 8 of the screws securing the bottom cover.
Lift off the bottom cover, being sure not to disconnect the cables for the L/R buttons on the back of the device.

steps.title: Lift the circle pad
lines: Use a JIS 00 screwdriver to remove the two screws securing the circle pad module.
The circle pad screws are slightly longer than the ones for the bottom cover.
Flip the circle pad over to expose its ZIF connector.
Using the tip of the spudger, gently lift off the lid of the ZIF connector to release the circle pad cable.
Take the new circle pad assembly and insert the cable back into the open ZIF connector and close it using the spudger.
Ensure the internal component of the circle pad is correctly oriented with a small screwdriver or spudger.
Gently place the new circle pad back into its place and secure with the screws.
We had to try this step a few times before we were able to orient it correctly. Try to make sure that the circle pad does not move the internal assembly once it is inserted.
